question: The printed price of a shirt is 800 and it is sold at a discount of 25%. Find the selling price of the shirt.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price = (100% − Discount%) of Marked Price

SP = (100% − 25%) of 800

SP = 75% of 800 = (3 ÷ 4) × 800

SP = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Printed price (MP) = ₹800

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 
 Marked Price

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 800 × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 800 × 75 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 8 × 75

⇒ SP = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the printed price or tag price of an article. Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price unless stated otherwise.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are given, the equivalent single discount is (x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100)%.

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
